source.title: On Gradient Descent Convergence beyond the Edge of Stability

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; figures are transcribed but their plotted values are not available as readable numbers.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether gradient descent can converge when the learning rate exceeds the edge-of-stability threshold, using theoretical analyses and experiments on toy objectives, teacher-student networks, matrix factorization, and MLPs on MNIST. This conceptually tests parts of V5, but not the squared-loss wide-network setting or sharpness-hovers claim as worded.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on period-2 and period-4 orbits, a high-dimensional teacher-student network, matrix factorization, and MLPs on MNIST. These results bear on V5's broader question of training beyond a stability threshold, but the paper does not test the claim's specified squared-loss wide-network behavior, sharpness hovers at the threshold, or divergence from rates below it. CIFAR and the other listed versions are not tested. Introductory reports of prior work are cited findings, not rows. MNIST figure curves are figure-only and have no textual numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own full-batch neural-network experiments beyond the stability threshold, including training-loss and sharpness measurements in synthetic ReLU networks and MNIST MLPs. These bear on V5 in new settings. Periodic-orbit proofs for scalar objectives and matrix factorization do not themselves establish V5's neural-network loss and sharpness behavior.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct, but generic higher-order conditions establish existence of two-step fixed points, not general convergence to them. Convergence is established in specific scalar and single-neuron settings. Matrix-factorization period-2 convergence is presented as observations with theoretical intuition and acknowledged proof gaps.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines non-asymptotic GD beyond the edge of stability in toy functions, a population-loss single-neuron model, matrix factorization, and synthetic/MNIST experiments. It does not reproduce the specified wide-network squared-loss experiments or measure their stated outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the orbit type and divergence behavior; initialization and matrix-factorization spectrum constrain the reported convergence; the MLP plots distinguish beyond-EoS epochs and layer counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Scalar objectives admit stable period-2 orbits beyond local stability, with period doubling at larger rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the analyzed scalar objectives, GD can approach periodic orbits beyond the local stability threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Beyond-threshold training balances scalar factors and aligns a single ReLU student neuron with its teacher while its weights oscillate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated initialization and learning-rate conditions, large-step GD produces balancing and teacher alignment in these simple models.

fits_no_version.finding: Matrix factorization exhibits periodic, chaotic, or divergent dynamics depending on learning rate, spectrum, and initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Beyond-threshold matrix-factorization dynamics depend on coupled spectral and initialization conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST MLP experiments associate beyond-EoS epochs with gradient alignment and a positive higher-derivative condition; the prose extends these observations to four and five layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested MNIST MLPs, local geometry during beyond-EoS training is consistent with the authors' one-dimensional oscillation analysis.

record.problems: The MNIST MLP outcome details are primarily in figures; exact numerical values are not given in the text. The MNIST experiment uses a simplified subset of 2,000 images from two classes and MSE loss, so it does not test classification training error on CIFAR. The matrix-factorization results include observations the authors say are difficult to prove rigorously, and the quasi-symmetric observation explicitly has proof gaps. The paper reports no uncertainty intervals or error bars for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No reported text result bearing on the tested V5 conditions was omitted. Figure 1's individual grid-search outcomes are not recoverable from the supplied figure transcription and remain figure-only in R10; Figures 8–11 are represented only where prose provides an outcome, with per-figure MNIST metrics retained as figure-only rows where no textual values are stated.

untested.parts: CIFAR convolutional-network training error, random or corrupted labels, and the specified size and training-recipe comparisons.
Spurious-local-minimum frequencies with increasing teacher/student width and additional student neurons.
Depth degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts, special initialization, or Fixup.
Initialization comparisons for training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.

The specified wide-network catapult sequence relative to the initial linearized model, its larger-rate divergence boundary, and divergence despite starting below the stability threshold. The neural-network loss/sharpness plots test the full-batch clause, but their outcomes remain unreadable in the supplied transcription.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup's speed and stability without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is justified by the readable linked outcomes: R11 establishes only part of V5's trajectory, and R13–R14 have unreadable behavioral curves. Missing curve details were already declared in rows_left_out. Period-4 or chaotic behavior does not challenge V5 merely because it differs from period-2 convergence.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification training, corrupted or random labels, model size effects, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU local minima frequency as teacher and student width grow, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth-dependent classification training error, and shortcut effects.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, training speed by initialization, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.

The paper studies GD beyond an edge-of-stability threshold, but not the specified wide-network squared-loss catapult experiment, curvature dropping during a loss rise, long-run sharpness hovering at the threshold, or runs that diverge from below it. Its experiments instead cover other toy and matrix-factorization dynamics, a synthetic teacher-student network, and MNIST MLPs.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, its effect on speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

rows.subject: f(x) = 1/4 (x^2 − μ)^2
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with η = K·μ⁻¹ from an initialization between 0 and √μ converges to a period-2 orbit.

conditions.value: any point 0 < x₀ < √μ, except a measure-zero initialization

rows.value: Converges to an orbit of period 2, except for a measure-zero initialization where it converges to √μ.
rows.note: The paper calls this a beyond-EoS learning rate and states the theorem's convergence result.
rows.check: The theorem establishes a scalar objective's period-2 orbit, not the neural-network training behavior specified by V5.

rows.subject: f(x) = 1/2 (xy − μ)^2
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with positive x and y throughout training; |x − y| decays on points where xy > μ.

conditions.value: both x and y are always positive during the whole process

rows.measure: Difference |x − y| on points where xy > μ
rows.note: This result is a balancing effect, not a classification-error measurement.
rows.check: Parameter balancing in scalar factorization does not measure V5's loss recovery or sharpness trajectory.

rows.subject: two-layer single-neuron ReLU network
rows.size_stated: one student neuron; input dimension d
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent under population L2 loss; theorem bounds decay of the off-teacher-direction component wy.
rows.note: The paper states convergence to a period-2 orbit separately in Proposition 4; this theorem's reported measure is decay of wy.
rows.check: Teacher-direction alignment does not establish loss recovery or sharpness hovering. Initialization should read ||w^(0)|| = v^(0) = epsilon, rather than equating a vector with a scalar. The T1 bound also requires a ceiling.

rows.subject: two-layer single-neuron model in Theorem 4
rows.size_stated: one student neuron; input dimension d
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent converges to a period-2 orbit with wy = 0.
rows.value: Converges to a period-2 orbit where wy = 0 and (v, wx) ∈ γK.
rows.note: The theorem and proposition state population-loss convergence; Appendix B.1 separately reports an empirical-loss experiment.
rows.check: A single neuron's convergence to a parameter orbit does not establish the specified wide-network catapult dynamics or continuing loss decrease at the stability threshold.

rows.subject: Matrix Factorization
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from a non-measure-zero set of initializations converges to a period-2 orbit.
rows.value: There exists non-measure-zero initialization from which GD converges to a period-2 orbit.
rows.note: The paper calls this an observation and says it is difficult to prove rigorously.
rows.check: Matrix-factorization orbit convergence concerns a different system and outcome. This is an observation with incomplete proof, not a proved convergence theorem.

rows.subject: Quasi-symmetric Matrix Factorization
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from a perturbed, unbalanced minimum converges approximately to a period-2 orbit.

conditions.value: near (Y₀ = αX₀, Z₀ = X₀/α), α > 0; deviations bounded by ϵ

rows.value: GD would converge to a period-2 orbit γη approximately with error in O(ϵ).
rows.note: The paper explicitly says a rigorous proof is missing; it presents this as an observation with intuition.
rows.check: Approximate matrix-factorization orbit convergence does not measure a claim version. The observation requires small perturbations; Appendix J.2 additionally specifies nonzero leading-direction perturbations and acknowledges proof gaps.

rows.subject: Matrix Factorization with generic initialization
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent is run at different learning rates; the paper reports orbit type by ησ₁².
rows.note: The stated interval and orbit type are reported in prose.
rows.check: Matrix-factorization orbit type does not establish V5's neural-network loss and sharpness dynamics.

rows.subject: Matrix Factorization with generic initialization
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent is run at different learning rates; the paper reports orbit type by ησ₁².
rows.value: Converges to a period-4 orbit, although the period-2 orbit still exists once ησ₁² < 1.5.
rows.note: This qualifies convergence to a period-2 orbit: its existence does not guarantee convergence.
rows.check: Period-4 behavior qualifies the paper's period-2 result, not V5. V5 does not predict period-2 convergence.

rows.subject: Matrix Factorization with generic initialization
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent is run at different learning rates; the paper reports dynamics by ησ₁².
rows.note: The text describes dynamics as chaotic without quantifying their training loss.
rows.check: Chaotic matrix-factorization dynamics are not evidence of neural-network divergence or failure to recover low training loss.

rows.subject: Matrix Factorization, different learning rates
rows.operation_detail: Learning rate is varied in experiments; the paper reports whether GD diverges and compares outcomes with a predicted boundary.

conditions.value: grid search over ησ₁² and ησ₂²
generic, quasi-symmetric α = 0.9, and symmetric α = 1

rows.measure: Divergence versus finite behavior across learning rates
rows.note: The prose says Figure 1 verifies the stated sufficient conditions and that the empirical boundary approximates linearity; it does not give readable individual outcomes.
rows.check: The divergence grid concerns matrix factorization. Its qualitative boundary is described in the text, but it does not test the systems specified by V5.

rows.subject: 2-layer 16-neuron teacher-student ReLU network
rows.size_stated: 16 student neurons; input x ∈ R¹⁶; 10,000 data points
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent trains the student network on sampled teacher-student data at two learning rates; a third run decays the larger rate after 100 epochs.

conditions.value: 100 epochs, then 20 additional epochs with decay from 2.6 to 0.5 for the decayed-rate run
same initialization; wi = ki(ei + 0.01ϵ), ki = 1 + 0.0625(i − 1), ϵ ∼ N(0, I)
10,000 points uniformly sampled from unit sphere S¹⁵

rows.baseline: η = 0.5 remains around sharp minima according to the text
rows.value: η = 2.6 drives to flatter minima and GD stably oscillates there; after decay, it converges to a nearby minimum significantly flatter than the η = 0.5 run.
rows.note: The paper explicitly states these qualitative results; the figure contains the curves.
rows.check: The text establishes flattening and stable oscillation at eta = 2.6 versus an approximately 2.5 threshold, followed by convergence after rate decay. It does not establish the complete initial loss-rise/curvature-drop/low-loss sequence or long-run sharpness hovering with continuing loss decrease.

rows.subject: 3-layer ReLU MLP on MNIST
rows.size_stated: 3 layers; 16 neurons per layer; 2,000 images from classes 0 and 1; input dimension 79
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent trains with MSE loss; the text reports alignment and a cross-section derivative condition during beyond-EoS epochs.

conditions.value: η = 0.5 for the reported alignment and derivative analyses
MNIST, 2,000 images from classes 0 and 1; significant input channels only

rows.measure: Cosine similarity between top Hessian eigenvector v₁ and gradient; sign of 3[f⁽³⁾]² − f⁽²⁾f⁽⁴⁾ at line-search minima
rows.value: Cosine similarity is pretty close to 1 during the stated beyond-EoS periods; most points have 3[f⁽³⁾]² − f⁽²⁾f⁽⁴⁾ > 0 except a few points, all outside the EoS regime.
rows.note: These are geometric conditions relevant to the authors' theory, not training classification error or direct convergence-to-low-loss results.
rows.check: The recorded measures are gradient alignment and a higher-derivative condition, which cannot establish V5's behavioral trajectory. Exceptions outside the EoS regime do not limit V5. The cosine result concerns absolute cosine similarity.

rows.subject: f(x) = 1/4 (x² − 1)²
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from near a period-2 orbit is analyzed and illustrated at three learning rates; at the largest rate the orbit type changes.
rows.value: η = 1.05 and 1.235 converge to period-2 orbits; η = 1.237 converges to a period-4 orbit.
rows.locator: Appendix L, Figure 12 and accompanying text
rows.note: The text identifies orbit types and gives a transition bound of √5 − 1 ≈ 1.236; this refines the conditions for period-2 convergence.
rows.check: The scalar period-doubling transition does not test a claim version. Initialization is described as near the period-2 orbit, rather than wholly unspecified.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Toy scalar objective and two-layer single-neuron ReLU population-loss setting
reader_labels.reason: Beyond-threshold GD converges to period-2 orbits in the scalar case and in the single-neuron setting (R1, R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Matrix factorization and tested learning-rate ranges
reader_labels.reason: Period-2 convergence occurs only in some reported ranges; higher rates yield period-4 or chaotic behavior, and the period-2 orbit can exist without being the converged orbit (R7–R9, R15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Most sampled line-search minima satisfy the paper's derivative condition, but a few do not, and the paper notes approximation error as a possible cause; these are theory diagnostics, not the version's specified training-loss behavior (R12).
